DAMGHANI:v1p285/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p285/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p285/r1.claim: The entry cites the cry that seized the people at sunrise.
DAMGHANI:v1p285/r1.anchor: وقال سبحانه في سورة الحجر فاخذتهم الصيحة مشرقين الثاني الصيحة يعني النفخة الاولى

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r1.claim: At dawn or an unexpected hour, a terrible cry overtook the people; their land was ruined and stones of baked clay rained down on them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r1.anchor: Ardından ülkeleri harap oldu, üzerlerine pişmiş çamurdan oluşan taşlar yağdı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r2.claim: Their fate illustrates what befalls a people who defy God, disregard a prophet’s warnings and moral values, and persist shamelessly in disgraceful immorality.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r2.anchor: Allah’a âsi olup peygamberin ikazlarını ciddiye almadan, hiçbir değer yargısı tanımadan, yüz kızartıcı ahlâksızlıkları bile hayasızca ve fütursuzca işlemekte ısrar eden bir toplumun âkıbeti ortaya konmuştur

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Ṣayhah means a shout and here denotes the punishment that overtook Lot's people at daybreak.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: means “a shout.” Here it refers to God’s punishment that visited the people of Lot (sws) as soon as it was daybreak.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The storm wind's thunder and lightning explain why the author considers the word ṣayhah apt for the punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The stormy wind was accompanied with the roar and glare of thunder and lightening.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r10.claim: الصيحة is the cry of destruction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r10.anchor: والصيحة: صيحة الهلاك. وقيل: صوت جبريل عليه السلام.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r11.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r11.claim: Another view identifies the cry as Gabriel’s voice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r11.anchor: والصيحة: صيحة الهلاك. وقيل: صوت جبريل عليه السلام.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r12.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls it the cry of terror and says it was unlike the cry that struck Thamud.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: هي صيحة الوحشة، وليست كصيحة ثمود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r13.claim: مشرقين means entering the time of sunrise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r13.anchor: مشرقين: داخلين في الشروق، وهو بزوغ الشمس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r14.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r14.claim: Another explanation says the punishment began at dawn and continued until sunrise, when the destruction was complete.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r14.anchor: وقيل: أول العذاب كان عند الصبح، وامتد إلى شروق الشمس، فكأنه تمام الهلاك عند ذلك.

QUSHAYRI:v2p142/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p142/r1.speaker: قوم
QUSHAYRI:v2p142/r1.claim: Some say Lot offered his own daughters to the people to turn them away from their vile intention, but they ignored his counsel.
QUSHAYRI:v2p142/r1.anchor: وقال قوم : أراد بناته من صلبه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r1.claim: The cry struck Lot's people in the morning; punishment began at daybreak and was complete at sunrise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r1.anchor: أي: حين أضاءت الشمس، فكان ابتداء العذاب حين أصبحوا،

BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r1.claim: The terrifying cry seized Lot’s people at daybreak; a ṣayḥa is a forceful voice so overwhelming that other sounds are negligible beside it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r1.anchor: فأخذتهم } أي أخذ انتقام وغلبة { الصيحة } أي التي هي لعظمها وهولها هي الصيحة , وغيرها عدم بالنسبة إليها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r2.claim: Mushriqīn means entering the brightness of sunrise; the term also shows that ṣubḥ and ṣabāḥ name the beginning of day, perhaps extending toward midday.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r2.anchor: مشرقين * } أي داخلين في الإشراق , وهو ضياء الشمس عند بزوغها , وتبين به أن وقته يسمى صبحا لغة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r3.claim: The cry may have come at sunrise as their end, while uprooting the cities at dawn began the destruction; the city tops were turned below and stones rained on their inhabitants, unlike the pronoun reference in Hud.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r3.anchor: أعاد الضمير على المعذبين لا على مدنهم - كما مضى في سورة هود عليه السلام - لأن هذا أصرح

DURR-FULL:v5p90/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p90/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v5p90/r4.claim: The cry was like a thunderbolt; anything that destroys a people may be called either a thunderbolt or a cry.
DURR-FULL:v5p90/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {فأخذتهم الصيحة} قال: {الصيحة} مثل الصاعقة كل شيء أهلك به قوم فهو صاعقة وصيحة

DURR-FULL:v5p90/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p90/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v5p90/r5.claim: “At sunrise” means when the sun had risen.
DURR-FULL:v5p90/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {مشرقين} قال: حين أشرقت الشمس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r6.claim: The sound’s seizure of them at sunrise follows from the prior decree; the ṣayḥa is a blast in the air involving thunderbolts, earthquakes, and stones of baked clay, as discussed in Hud.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r6.anchor: وجملة فأخذتهم الصيحة مشرقين } تفريع على جملة { وقضينا إليه ذلك الأمر ( سورة الحجر : 66 ) . والصيحة } : صعقة في الهواء ، وهي صواعق وزلازل وفيها حجارة من سجيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r7.claim: Mushriqīn is an accusative circumstantial participle from the plural verb, meaning they had entered the sunrise time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r7.anchor: وانتصب { مشرقين } على الحال من ضمير الغيبة . وهو اسم فاعل من أشرقوا إذا دخلوا في وقت شروق الشمس .

JISHUMI:v6p3969/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3969/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3969/r5.claim: Al-ṣayḥa is a loud, forceful sound.

JISHUMI:v6p3969/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3969/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3969/r6.claim: Ishrāq is daylight or brightness at sunrise: sharaqat is when the sun rises, while ashraqat is when it shines and clears.
JISHUMI:v6p3969/r6.anchor: والإشراق: ضياء الشمس بالنهار، شرقت الشمس تشرق شروقا إذا طلعت، وأشرقت إشراقا إذا أضاءت وصفت

JISHUMI:v6p3969/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3969/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3969/r7.claim: Mushriqīn is accusative as a circumstantial phrase, describing the punishment at sunrise.
JISHUMI:v6p3969/r7.anchor: مشرقين نصب على الحال أي: العذاب في حال الشروق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r16.claim: “At sunrise” means entering the time when the sun rises.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r16.anchor: داخلين في الشروق وهو بزوع الشمس

QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r1.claim: Mushriqin is a circumstantial accusative meaning that the cry struck them at sunrise.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r1.anchor: { فأخذتهم الصيحة مشرقين } نصب على الحال، أي وقت شروق الشمس.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r2.claim: Ashraqat means the sun shone, while sharqat means it rose; some regard the two as synonymous.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r2.anchor: يقال: أشرقت الشمس أي أضاءت، وشرقت إذا طلعت. وقيل: هما لغتان بمعنى.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r3.claim: The intended meaning may be that the people entered sunrise time, as one says they entered morning or evening.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r3.anchor: وأشرق القوم أي دخلوا في وقت شروق الشمس. مثل أصبحوا وأمسوا، وهو المراد في الآية.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r4.claim: Other views place the beginning of the punishment at dawn and its completion at sunrise, or identify the time as daybreak.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r4.anchor: وقيل: أول العذاب كان عند الصبح وامتد إلى شروق الشمس، فكان تمام الهلاك عند ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:73-74/r5.claim: The cry means the punishment; the discussion of sijjil appeared earlier.

RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r1.speaker: أهل المعاني
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r1.claim: Ahl al-Maʿānī say the verse does not itself establish that the deadly cry was Gabriel's; that identification needs strong external proof.
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r1.anchor: قال أهل المعاني : ليس في الآية دلالة على أن تلك الصيحة صيحة جبريل عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r2.claim: Without strong evidence for Gabriel's role, the verse only shows that a tremendous, deadly cry came upon them.
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r2.anchor: وإلا فليس في الآية دلالة إلا على أنه جاءتهم صيحة عظيمة مهلكة

RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r3.claim: Mushriqīn means entering sunrise, the rising of the sun; the root can describe anything that appears from the east.
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r3.anchor: يقال شرق الشارق يشرق شروقا لكل ما طلع من جانب الشرق

STUDYQURAN:15:73/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:73/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:73/r1.claim: The account of Lot’s people here is tied to the commentary on 11:82–83.

THALABI:v5p345/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p345/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p345/r15.claim: The morning description means the sun had risen and brightened; the word is parsed as a circumstantial accusative.
THALABI:v5p345/r15.anchor: حيث أشرقت الشمس، أي أضاءت، وهو نصب على الحال

TAB-FULL:v14p93/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p93/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p93/r1.claim: The cry was a thunderbolt of punishment that struck them as the sun rose; “they were cried out against” means they were destroyed.

TAB-FULL:v14p93/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p93/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p93/r2.claim: Mushriqīn and muṣbiḥīn are accusative circumstantial expressions meaning that they were at sunrise or morning.

TAB-FULL:v14p93/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p93/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v14p93/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says they were struck when the sun had risen, which is what “at sunrise” means.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r1.claim: The cry is the cry of punishment; the commentators say Gabriel cried out against Lot’s people and destroyed them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r1.anchor: يعني صيحة العذاب، قال المفسرون: صاح بهم جبريل صيحة أهلكتهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r2.claim: The semanticists offer an alternative: a great sound produced by God may have come upon them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r2.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: ويجوز أن يكون جاءهم صوت عظيم من فعل الله عز وجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r3.claim: The root can describe anything rising from the east, including dawn, stars, sun, or moon; “the sun shone” means it brightened after rising, and “the people entered sunrise” parallels saying they entered morning or evening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r3.anchor: يقال: شرق الشارق يشرق شروقا، لكل ما طلع من جانب الشرق، ومنه قولهم: ما ذر شارق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r4.speaker: المفسرون والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r4.claim: Most commentators take mushriqīn to mean entering sunrise; al-Zajjaj specifies that they encountered the rising of the sun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r4.anchor: والمفسرون على هذا في قوله: {مشرقين} قالوا: داخلين في الإشراق (¬1). وقال الزجاج: مصادفين لطلوع الشمس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r5.claim: Asked how this fits the promise that Lot’s people would be destroyed at daybreak, some semanticists equate sunrise with dawn; others say punishment began at dawn and destruction was complete at sunrise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p636/r5.anchor: قيل إن جماعة من أهل المعاني قالوا في معنى {مشرقين}: مصبحين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:67-73/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:67-73/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:67-73/r10.claim: Gabriel cried out at them with a cry that destroyed them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:67-73/r10.anchor: صاح بهم جبريل عليه السلام صيحة أهلكتهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:67-73/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:67-73/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:67-73/r11.claim: They were struck at sunrise, when the destruction was completed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:67-73/r11.anchor: داخلين في وقت شروق الشمس، وذلك أن تمام الهلاك كان مع الإشراق

SAMIN-DURR:15:73/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:15:73/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:15:73/r1.claim: مشرقين is a circumstantial accusative describing the people seized: they were entering the sunrise.

ZAJJAJ:v3p183/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p183/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p183/r5.claim: The cry of punishment seized Lot's people when they encountered sunrise.
ZAJJAJ:v3p183/r5.anchor: أي أخذت قوم لوط الصيحة بالعذاب مشرقين

ZAJJAJ:v3p183/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p183/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p183/r6.claim: Ashraqnā means that people met the sunrise, just as aṣbaḥnā means that they met the morning.

ZAJJAJ:v3p183/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p183/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p183/r7.claim: The sun's rising can be expressed with either sharaqat or ashraqat; here mushriqīn specifically means coinciding with sunrise.
ZAJJAJ:v3p183/r7.anchor: يقال شرقت الشمس إذا طلعت وأشرقت بمعنى واحد

ASAD-NOTES:15:73#n52/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:73#n52/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:73#n52/r1.claim: Asad translates sayhah as a blast of God's punishment and refers readers to his discussion at surah 11, note 98.
ASAD-NOTES:15:73#n52/r1.anchor: term sayhah, rendered by me as "blast of [God's punishment"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p914/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p914/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p914/r3.claim: The punishment in al-Hijr is harsher: the cry at sunrise, overturning of the city, and stones of baked clay exceed the rain punishment mentioned in al-Naml.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p914/r3.anchor: لوجدنا أن العقوبة في سورة الحجر أشدّ

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī first glosses the ṣayḥa as a tremendous cry and takes the definite article as generic.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r2.claim: Another view identifies the cry as Gabriel’s, with the definite article referring to a known event.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r2.anchor: وقيل : صيحة جبريل عليه السلام فالتعريف للعهد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r3.claim: The Imam says the verse itself does not identify Gabriel; accept that only if strong evidence establishes it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r3.anchor: وقال الإمام : ليس في الآية دلالة على هذا التعيين فإن ثبت بدليل قوي قيل به

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the cry was like a thunderbolt; any means by which a people are destroyed may be called ṣāʿiqa and ṣayḥa.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج أنه قال في الآية : الصيحة مثل الصاعقة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r5.claim: Mushriqīn means entering the time of sunrise.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r5.anchor: داخلين في وقت شروق الشمس قال المدقق

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r6.speaker: المدقق
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r6.claim: Al-Mudaqqiq reconciles ‘at dawn’ and ‘at sunrise’ by making dawn the punishment’s beginning and sunrise its end.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r6.anchor: والجمع بين مصبحين ومشرقين باعتبار الابتداء والانتهاء بأن يكون ابتداء العذاب عند الصبح وانتهاؤه عند الشروق

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r7.claim: The cry seized them by overpowering and taking control; akhīdh can also mean a captive.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r7.anchor: وأخذ الصيحة قهرها إياهم وتمكنها منهم ومنه الأخيذ الأسير

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r8.claim: A gloss takes maqṭūʿ to mean ‘soon to be cut off.’
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r8.anchor: ولك أن تقول : ( مقطوع ) بمعنى يقطع عما قريب

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74/r9.claim: Another gloss parses mushriqīn as a prospective circumstantial state.

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:73/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:73/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:73/r1.claim: The people were seized by a terrifying, deadly blast; it is also said to have been Gabriel's cry.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:73/r1.anchor: يعني صيحة هائلة مهلكة. وقيل صيحة جبريل عليه السلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:73/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:73/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:73/r2.claim: They were struck as they entered the time of sunrise.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r1.claim: This was the sudden blast of impact, unlike the blast of Thamud; they were destroyed after dawn, with annihilation completed at sunrise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r1.anchor: وهذه «الصيحة» هي صيحة الوجبة وليست كصيحة ثمود، وأهلكوا بعد الفجر مصبحين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r1.claim: The cry that seized them was the cry of punishment, namely Gabriel's cry.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r1.anchor: ( فأخذتهم الصيحة ) يعني صيحة العذاب وهي صيحة جبريل عليه السلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says ashraqū means they encountered sunrise; shariqat means the sun rose, while ashraqat means it shone, though some use both verbs alike.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج يقال أشرقنا فنحن مشرقون إذا صادفوا شروق الشمس وهو طلوعها كما يقال أصبحنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r3.claim: In this verse, mushriqīn means that they were caught at the time of sunrise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409/r3.anchor: إلا أن مشرقين في معنى مصادفين لطلوع الشمس

MUQATIL:15:67-73/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:15:67-73/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:15:67-73/r8.claim: The cry was Gabriel's cry, and it struck them at sunrise.
MUQATIL:15:67-73/r8.anchor: يعني صيحة جبريل، عليه السلام، { مشرقين } [آية: 73] يعني حين طلعت الشمس

NASAFI-FULL:v2p245#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p245#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p245#8/r1.claim: The cry was the cry of Gabriel.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p245#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p245#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p245#8/r2.claim: They were entering sunrise, when the sun rose.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p245#8/r2.anchor: ﴿ فأخذتهم الصيحة ﴾ صيحة جبريل عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v4p319/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p319/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p319/r3.claim: Those seized are the people of Lot, and the cry is the shout of Gabriel.
BURSEVI:v4p319/r3.anchor: {فأخذتهم} أي قوم لوط الصيحة أي : صيحة جبريل عليه السلام.

BURSEVI:v4p319/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p319/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p319/r4.claim: مشرقين means entering the time of sunrise; the punishment began at morning and was complete when the sun rose.
BURSEVI:v4p319/r4.anchor: مشرقين أي حال كونهم داخلين في وقت شروق الشمس

BURSEVI:v4p319/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p319/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p319/r5.claim: The report that the people were cut off at morning (15:66) describes the beginning, while مشرقين marks the completion when Gabriel lifted their towns, overturned them, and cried out.
BURSEVI:v4p319/r5.anchor: وتمامه حين أشرقوا لأن جبريل قلع الأرضين بهم

BURSEVI:v4p319/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p319/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p319/r6.claim: The active and passive participles describe the event as it is happening, not after it ends; using مقطوع after completion would be figurative for about to be cut off.
BURSEVI:v4p319/r6.anchor: وذلك أن تقول مقطوع بمعنى بقطع عن قريب
